newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.

text.p: Early calls on both CME live and feeder cattle futures ranged 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower as as markets await Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report, traders said.
Trade is expected to be lightly mixed in both pits as traders square positions in front of the report. Daily market factors may have little effect on the market, analysts said.

However, some analysts expect markets to drift lower. They cited continued weakness in the boxed beef market as a bearish factor to live cattle while a lower CME feeder cattle index and calls for higher corn futures could press feeders.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.03 at $77.19 per cwt.

Analyst estimates on the Cattle-on-Feed report put June 1 total on-feed cattle supplies in the major 7-states at an average of 113.2 percent in a range of 111.5 to 114 percent of a year ago. A number at the high end would be a record high. Placement estimates averaged 117.2 in a range of 110.5 to 124 percent and marketings averaged 99 in a range of 97 to 100.5 percent.
